about: Every knit whose exact machine file is in the repository, oldest first, with what the operator reported and where. `studio knitted` reads new files against it. See README.md beside this file.

yarns.draw-thin: The thin draw thread on the machine; not identified

knits.what: Kniterate's own fairisle.kc, knitted as a control (issue #9 run 1)
knits.caveat: The two pattern yarns differed in thickness and the waste was a single thin strand; neither is established as the cause.

events.what: The black yarn (C4) broke at the start of the fairisle rows; the transition has large openings.
The black yarn broke in several more places afterwards; the report does not say where.

knits.report: Run 2 — completed, better matching stitches, startup/transition problems remain

events.what: The waste yarn's first row did not catch; the second row caught the loose span and tangled. The operator paused, cleared it and carried on.
The draw thread sometimes missed its whole first pass; later passes worked.
Yarn broke at the first fairisle row.

knits.what: Mini toque with a bird, as issued (issue #9 run 3); stopped at the start
knits.report: The original faster Run 3 attempt had missed knitting near the beginning needles and waste-yarn tangling during C3/C4 introduction.
knits.caveat: The pass it stopped at was not recorded. It stopped during waste; no completed prefix is confirmed and no pass is credited from this run.

events.what: Stitches were missed near the first needles and the waste yarn tangled while the two body yarns were brought in. The run was stopped.

knits.what: The same mini toque with every pass at speed 100, edited by the operator; completed
knits.report: Run 3 completed successfully as a construction trial at speed 100: the 2×2 cast-on looks neat and needle movement worked well. There are still edge drops and finishing/fabric issues to address.
knits.caveat: Not a file Studio made: the issued toque with every pass set to speed 100. The bytes were rebuilt from the issued file and match the hash the operator reported.

events.what: Occasional drops at the left edge while the waste was knitted.
Occasional drops at the right edge during the jacquard rows.
The crown is tight and stiff, and the bird is too small to read.

knits.what: Studio's fairisle chart with the yarn catch, 64 columns (issue #9 handoff 2, run 2)
knits.report: Knitted to the end; the operator called it the best fabric so far.

events.what: On the first main-yarn row after the waste, the yarn looked cut or broken and frayed at the bottom-left corner.
The edge where a carrier turns looks a little loose.

knits.what: One-colour strip with a chain bind-off, first cast-on row at roller 300 (the operator's run 4B)
knits.report: Main yarn broke during the first left-to-right return, at the bottom left. Bind-off mostly worked, with broken yarn at its right-hand starting edge.
knits.caveat: The file is the operator's, copied from their records pull request at commit 86ee485.

events.what: The main yarn broke during the first left-to-right return, at the bottom left.
The bind-off broke the yarn at its right-hand starting edge; the rest of it mostly worked.

knits.what: The operator's first reversible rectangle; aborted at the start
knits.report: Aborted: C1 missed its first arrival from the left, C6 tangled; C3 caught the oldest waste row
knits.caveat: The pass it stopped at was not recorded. It stopped during waste; no completed prefix is confirmed and no pass is credited from this run. The file is the operator's, copied from their records pull request at commit 86ee485.

events.what: The draw thread missed its first arrival from the left, the waste yarn tangled, and orange caught the oldest waste row. The run was aborted.

knits.what: The operator's second reversible rectangle, 62 columns; completed
knits.report: Completed rectangle; C1 caught successfully, previous startup issue not observed; open cast-on edge and orange reverse setup band remain
knits.caveat: The file is the operator's, copied from their records pull request at commit 86ee485.

events.what: The lower edge is open, with regularly spaced holes, and about four orange rows show on the grey face before its grey starts. The operator found the edge unacceptable.

knits.what: One-colour strip ending in a chain bind-off (issue #9 handoff 3, strip 2)
knits.report: Completed without apparent cast-on or bind-off breaks.

events.what: The waste missed early, around the third row shown on the machine.
A stitch at the left edge failed to establish through the body.

knits.what: Reversible two-colour rectangle with paisleys, 68 columns, from Studio's normal export
knits.caveat: Stops and interventions were not individually reported.

knits.what: Reversible diamond 16 to 48 to 16 columns, with the older increase
knits.report: A finished diamond with repeated stops; not a clean run.
knits.caveat: How many stops, and at which passes, was not recorded.

events.what: Repeated stops, reported as 'crump' (likely CLUMP), while the waste and draw feeders were being moved.
Increase edges look open, with orange bars on the grey face; decreases look satisfactory.

knits.what: One-colour jersey strip comparing four increases, 40 columns (538 passes); stopped in an unrecorded band
knits.report: had to stop it. post photo with this on gh. the increase was ~ok except it missed the last loop. the decrease (i guess its doing fashion decrease?) was bad. also i think the swatch can be smaller.
knits.caveat: Neither the stop pass nor the band reached was recorded. Body observations confirm completion of the startup only (through pass 116); no body pass is credited from this run.

events.what: The increase missed its last loop and the decrease was bad. The operator stopped the run; the band and stop pass were not recorded.

knits.what: One-colour jersey swatch, 40 columns, narrowing and widening at both edges
knits.report: this test knit was successuful on dec/inc and main yarn cast on part
knits.caveat: No stop or intervention log was supplied.

knits.what: Reversible paisley 8 to 21 to 8 columns, with the older increase
knits.caveat: Known from one photo of one face: a finished piece with all three motifs and no ladder visible. That this file is the piece photographed is inferred from the photo and the last file issued. Nothing was said about how it ran.

events.what: The widening edge is stepped, with open or stretched-looking loops.

knits.what: One-colour jersey swatch widening with split stitches, 40 to 52 columns
knits.report: this looks better. the right side is better than left. Asked whether it finished without stops, repairs or setting changes: yes it worked well.

events.what: The right edge looks better than the left; not explained.

knits.what: Reversible strip 20 to 24 columns: split increase on the right edge, the older increase on the left
knits.report: here. the right side is better, but im not sure that's what you are calling right?
knits.caveat: The operator said how it looks, not how it ran. Only the grey face was photographed.

events.what: The split edge looks more compact and regular than the older increase on the other edge.

knits.what: Reversible paisley 8 to 21 to 8 columns with split increases (514 passes)

events.what: Waste stitches dropped twice while orange and grey were first brought in, before the rear waste loops are released at pass 105.
Orange shows on the grey face at every other increase. Placing it at the splits orange makes is our reading, not the operator's.
The increase looks less compact than the decrease.

knits.what: Reversible strip 16 to 18 columns with a same-colour increase and a tucked edge join (234 passes)
knits.report: the last increase did not seem to work very well. it looks bad. the prev was better. can you see it? i think you tried to make it gray but it didnt quite knit
knits.caveat: No failing pass was confirmed, and the photos supplied show an earlier piece.

events.what: The increase looked bad and the grey loop 'didnt quite knit'. The strip changed the increase and the edge join together, so the report cannot be placed on one of them: it counts against whatever was new in this strip.
